test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Surya participated in a marathon. From starting point he ran 11 km towards West, turned right and ran for 12 km and turned right again and ran 11 km and then turned right again and ran 9 km. How many kms he has to run now in order to reach the starting point from his present position to complete the marathon?
solution:
According to the given information:

From starting point he ran 11 km towards West, turned right and ran for 12 km and turned right again and ran 11 km and then turned right again and ran 9 km.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f09333ae9e281704aa025bcf42c7b1714f063b0df07a9fa84a76b9e5737c90d6.png] 

Distance between present position and starting point = 12 - 9 = 3 km.

So, he has to run **3 km **now in order to reach the starting point from his present position to complete the marathon.

Hence, the correct answer is** "3 km".**
